explanation: `terraform init -upgrade` tells Terraform to ignore the existing lock file and pick the newest provider version that still satisfies the version constraint — that is exactly what the flag is designed for. Deleting the lock file manually would work but is not the recommended approach and loses the hash records. `terraform apply` has no `-upgrade` flag for providers. Editing the lock file by hand would corrupt its checksums.

Without `-upgrade`, `terraform init` respects whatever version is already recorded in the lock file and does not re-select providers. You must pass `-upgrade` to have Terraform pick the newest version allowed by the updated constraint.

`terraform init` is explicitly documented as safe to run multiple times and will never delete existing configuration or state. The `-upgrade` flag affects only which provider (or module) version is downloaded and recorded in the lock file — state is untouched.
